component.name: AutoPaper
component.summary: New wallpapers from a few keywords

description.p: Give AutoPaper a few keywords instead of an image prompt, and it keeps making new wallpapers from them: it composes a scene, has it painted by the provider you choose, and sets it as your wallpaper. It remembers everything it has made, so you're unlikely to see the same idea twice.

ul.li: Keywords marked Must, Maybe or Avoid, and a Surprise setting from faithful to wild
Moods: named sets of keywords, each with its own Surprise, to switch between
Like and Dislike: AutoPaper learns what you enjoy
Memory with a quiet period you choose, and echoes: old ideas coming back in a new form
History of everything it made, with each echo linked to its original
Your own keys for OpenAI or Google Gemini, or local models (Ollama, ComfyUI, OpenAI-compatible servers)
A monthly budget, with estimated costs
No accounts, no telemetry, no AutoPaper server

description.p: A Demo mode makes colour gradients without any AI, for trying the app.

description.p: The first release of AutoPaper for Linux.

It makes a new wallpaper from your keywords on the schedule you choose, or when you ask, with OpenAI, Google Gemini, or a model on your own computer through Ollama, ComfyUI or an OpenAI-compatible server. Moods, Like and Dislike, memory with echoes, a history of everything it has made, and a monthly budget are all in this first version. On GNOME it runs in the background and tells you about new wallpapers with notifications; on KDE Plasma and other desktops it also has a tray icon.
